claims.text: The rider's own claim measures the trip at 16.91 km against a booked optimal of 15.1 km, and the platform's own derived deviation block confirms the trace distance is 16.91 km against the same 15.1 km optimal, an excess of 1.81 km. That excess is real and it is measured on the governing field, gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 makes the controlling figure over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 16.9 km.

The excess of 1.81 km is 11.99% of the 15.1 km optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal AND exceed 0.8 km absolute. The absolute test passes (1.81 km > 0.8 km) but the percentage test fails (11.99% < 20%). On the face of the trace, no route deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01, and the clause directs that where either establishment test fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. I concede this point: the measured excess does not clear the POL-RD-01 threshold.

The driver's explanation for the longer route is 'I followed the navigation.' That is a bare assertion of an external traffic cause with no evidence ID attached to it. POL-RD-13 requires such an assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. The assertion carries no weight.

No traffic advisory covers this trip at all. The artifact EV-ADVIS-02807-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own detail states no advisory covers the Tampines Mall corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run on the record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the driver's traffic excuse is weightless. The absence is itself citable and it is cited here.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes. It carries 133 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so it does not meet any of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs (no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds). The trace is therefore not impaired under POL-RD-07 and the case does not escalate under POL-RD-10(3).

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is met on the first limb: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-02807 and the same pickup timestamp of 2026-08-21T13:24:42+08:00, so the artifacts describe the same trip. The second limb, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, is not met on the measured figure, and I do not pretend otherwise.

The fare ledger shows the rider was charged SGD 23.44 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The platform's own recomputation against the booked optimal route produces a recomputed_fare of SGD 21.6370, a refund_before_rounding of SGD 1.8030, and a payable figure of SGD 1.85. That is the arithmetic POL-RD-02 would produce if a deviation were established, and it is the figure the rider is contesting.

The driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 350, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test is not met: the trailing-90-day flag count is below 3 and the ratio is 0.0, well under the 0.05 threshold. No repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral is available on this record. I note that prior_deviation_flags is 1, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 forbid substituting it for the trailing-window figure.

The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration gate for a low-excess claim is not triggered: the rider has not filed four or more claims in 60 days. The rider's claim is not penalised by that factor, but neither does it rescue a claim that fails the POL-RD-01 threshold on its own arithmetic.

The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero tolls, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route gantry charge and no airport surcharge to correct under POL-RD-09. The billing-integrity route under POL-RD-09(4) is unavailable because there is no unmatched charge line to refund.

The chat log for this trip is empty: message_count 0, no messages, no waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log with a waypoint_hint the trace can be tested against, and POL-RD-05 requires an amendment timestamp with a stored amended_optimal_distance_km. Neither exists here, so no rider-requested detour and no relocation can be run, and the driver cannot invoke either clause to excuse the excess.

The trip is not a pooled trip: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline for any threshold test is the booked optimal of 15.1 km, not a matched-itinerary figure.

The fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, and quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-11 does not apply, so the distance-and-time refund route is not closed by upfront pricing and POL-RD-02 is the correct arithmetic if a deviation were established. It is not established, because the percentage test fails.

The rider's claim text asserts the fare was higher than normal and the distance was 16.91 km instead of 15.1 km. The distance figure is accurate and is confirmed by the trace, but the legal consequence the rider seeks does not follow: POL-RD-01 sets a 20% gate that an 11.99% excess does not clear, and POL-RD-01 expressly directs NO_ACTION where either establishment test fails, however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's factual observation is correct; the remedy is not available on this record.

claims.text: The rider's own claim measures the trip at 16.91 km against a booked optimal of 15.1 km, and the governing trace figure confirms it: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 16.91 km, which is the field POL-RD-01 makes controlling over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 16.9 km. The excess is therefore 1.81 km, or 11.99% of optimal.

That excess fails both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test. The percentage limb requires an excess greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km; 11.99% does not reach it. The absolute limb requires an excess greater than 0.8 km; 1.81 km does clear that limb, but POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass, and one has failed. The derived deviation status on the trace is itself recorded as 'no deviation'.

Because the establishment test fails, POL-RD-01 directs that no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's assertion that the fare was 'higher than normal' is not a route deviation within the clause; the 1.81 km of extra distance is ordinary variation below the materiality gate the policy deliberately sets so that lane changes and forced U-turns never become refundable disputes.

The driver's account is corroborated rather than contradicted by the record. The driver stated 'I followed the navigation', and the trace shows a continuous, well-sampled run: 133 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, with speeds clustered in a normal 40-52 kph band and no stop-and-go pattern. Nothing in the trace shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor and rejoining it, which is the shape POL-RD-03 requires before a closure excuse could even be tested.

The rider's claim is not corroborated by any independent artifact. The chat log for this trip is empty - 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp - so there is no rider complaint in the moment and no instruction of any kind. The rider's only support is the distance figure itself, which is the same trace measurement the driver's route is judged on.

The fare ledger is internally consistent and shows no billing-integrity defect that could ground a refund independently of the deviation question. The trip is METERED, charged_total is 23.44 SGD, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. There are no ERP gantries on this trip and no airport surcharge line, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to correct under POL-RD-09(4).

The driver's profile does not support any adverse finding on this trip. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 350 completed trips in the same window, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test is nowhere near its threshold of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio. I note for completeness that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is 1, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 forbid substituting it for the trailing-90-day figure.

The rider's profile likewise gives no ground to discount the driver's position. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant is not engaged, and the rider's single prior dispute was not upheld. These are the only rider fields POL-RD-08 permits me to use for this test.

I concede the one point that runs against the driver: the trace does record 1.81 km more distance than the booked optimal route, and the rider did pay for it. I do not dispute the measurement. My case is that the policy sets a materiality gate this excess does not clear, and that the gate is the whole point of POL-RD-01 - a sub-threshold excess is not a deviation and produces NO_ACTION.

No traffic advisory is on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02807-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, the pre-pass recording that no advisory covers the Tampines Mall corridor in this window. That absence is citable, and it means no external-cause exoneration under POL-RD-03 is available to either side - but it also means the rider cannot point to any external event that would have forced a longer route, and the driver's clean, gap-free trace needs no excuse.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes as well as at schema level. It carries no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds - max_gap_sec is 0.0 and sample_interval_sec equals expected_interval_sec at 10.0. POL-RD-07 therefore does not trigger, no independent corroboration is required, and the trace stands as the deciding artifact at full weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your distance observation is accurate, but it does not clear the policy's gate. The governing measurement is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. The trace records 16.91 km (EV-GPS-02807) against a booked optimal route of 15.1 km (EV-TRIP-02807), an excess of 1.81 km, or 11.99% of optimal. The trace is clean: 133 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, so it is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 and stands at full weight 1.0.

POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must exceed 20% of the optimal route AND exceed 0.8 km. The absolute test passes (1.81 km), but the percentage test fails (11.99% is below 20%). Where either test fails, POL-RD-01 directs that no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The 1.81 km is ordinary route variation below the materiality gate the policy deliberately sets so that lane changes and forced U-turns do not become refundable disputes.

To the driver: your position is accepted on the threshold point, but not as an exoneration. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02807-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Your statement 'I followed the navigation' is not a traffic-cause assertion grounded in an advisory, and under POL-RD-13 the absent advisory makes any such excuse weightless. It neither reduces the measured excess nor escalates the case, because you did not invoke POL-RD-03 against a cited advisory.

Why the refund arithmetic does not run. POL-RD-02 would recompute the fare against the optimal route at about SGD 1.85 on a charged_total of SGD 23.44 (EV-FARE-02807), but that computation only operates once a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. It is not, so no distance-and-time refund is available. The fare is METERED with no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not close or open anything. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so there was no rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04) and no relocation with a stored amended optimal (POL-RD-05). The trip is RYDE_X, not pooled, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

Billing integrity. The fare ledger carries zero ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is no unmatched charge line, so no standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), and none of the three POL-RD-02 steps (23.44 charged, 21.6370 recomputed, 1.8030 before rounding) is payable.

Driver conduct. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 350, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test is not met and no FULL_REFUND uplift or driver-conduct referral follows. The lifetime counters on both profiles (prior_deviation_flags for the driver; prior_disputes_filed and prior_disputes_upheld for the rider) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used as a ground in either direction.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trip identifier TRP-02807 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown with a consistent pickup timestamp, and the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c).

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the charge stands as billed; no money moves and the contested SGD 1.50 is neither refunded nor re-collected. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

It carries no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds - max_gap_sec is 0.0 and sample_interval_sec equals expected_interval_sec at 10.0. POL-RD-07 therefore does not trigger, no independent corroboration is required, and the trace stands as the deciding artifact at full weight 1.0.
